subject: SIG evidence: commit signing, CI delegation, and secret rotation artifacts
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@assesspartners.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG request — artifacts for code authorship & CI delegation

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of the SIG assurance for Greenline Financial we need a compact evidence package that demonstrates: commit authorship (signed commits / commit provenance), PR gating (branch protection / required checks), CI delegation controls (who can run ephemeral runners, job IDs, and how job tokens are minted), and recent secrets rotation logs.

Can you provide the following items by EOD Thursday (2026-05-21)?
- A snapshot of recent signed commits (last 90 days) with SHAs and signature metadata (GPG key IDs or signer IDs).
- CI job identifiers and logs for the build and deploy pipelines that show gating checks (include job IDs & timestamps).
- Vault rotation evidence (KMS key rotation or transit logs) for short-lived tokens used by runners.
- A short narrative (~1 page) describing the change-approval workflow for hotfixes and emergency rollbacks.

Attachment guidance: small archives or CSV manifests are easiest. If anything is sensitive, we can accept redacted logs and preserve the original artifacts under a secure link.

Thanks — Elena
Security Assessment Team
Assess Partners


From: soojin.lee@redwood.com <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@assesspartners.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — artifacts for code authorship & CI delegation

Jonas / Marissa — looping you in to pull items for Assess Partners. Elena requested a tight package focused on: signed commits, CI job IDs showing gating, and vault rotation logs.

Plan I propose:
- Jonas: produce a CSV manifest with commit SHAs, author email, signature type (GPG vs. GitHub SSO), and verification status; include a small tarball with the commit objects we can share (signed-commits-snapshot.tar.gz).
- Marissa: export CI job meta for the last 90 days for main & release branches (ci-job-ids-2026-Q1.csv) and the Vault rotation log (vault-rotation-log-2026-04.pdf). Note: redact any user tokens.
- I will draft the narrative that explains PR gating, who can bypass, and our emergency workflow. Also will include links to the deployment-policy-ephemeral-runners.md doc and artifact manifest.

Timeline: can we have the draft artifacts by Wednesday morning so I can assemble and send to Elena on Thursday? If anything needs escalation to legal for redaction, flag it here.

Thanks — Soojin
Engineering Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG request — artifacts for code authorship & CI delegation

Soojin — attaching a compact manifest and notes.

What I pulled:
- artifact-manifest-20260520.csv (1) — a mapping of build artifact IDs to the producing job ID and commit SHA (artifact_id, job_id, commit_sha).
- signed-commits-snapshot.tar.gz (2) — contains a plain CSV of signed commit SHAs + metadata and a directory with PGP sigs exported for verification. The CSV columns: commit_sha, author_email, signature_scheme, signer_key_id, verification_status, timestamp.

Example rows (redacted here):
- 9f4d3b7a..., dev1@redwood.com, GPG, 0xA1B2C3D4, verified, 2026-04-11T15:22:10Z
- 3b7a1c9d..., infra-bot@redwood.com, GitHub-SAML, internal-sso, verified, 2026-03-02T02:04:01Z

Notes on verification: most production merges are GPG or GitHub SAML-signed; we record signer metadata in git-notes for each merge commit. I included a README in the tar that explains verification steps (gpg --verify and our git-notes mapping).

I also exported the raw CI job IDs we've been asked for into ci-job-ids-2026-Q1.csv. Each row includes job_id, pipeline_name, status, triggered_by, runner_label, start_ts, end_ts. For gating checks look at pipeline_name: release/prod-verify and required checks list.

Let me know if you want the full raw logs (they're ~120MB). I can provide a redacted subset.

— Jonas
Build & Release Engineer

Quick update on the secrets & runner side.

What I'm attaching:
- vault-rotation-log-2026-04.pdf — redacted rotation events for the KMS and transit keys used by CI (shows rotation timestamps, key IDs, and internal request IDs).
- deployment-policy-ephemeral-runners.md — current policy describing who may register ephemeral runners, the required label/permission set, and our job-token TTL (currently 5m with automatic exchange).

A few clarifications for the assessor:
- Runner enrollment: only the infra team (infra-admins group) can approve runner registration; we have an automated enrollment that writes a short-lived credential to Vault and requires a human approval event in the change board for any long-lived runner.
- Job tokens: minted by the CI control plane with limited scope; tokens are audited in the transit logs we exported. We rotate the signing keys quarterly and keep a 30-day rotation history in the report.
- Emergency change flow: small excerpt below — emergency PRs must be marked with the label emergency/hotfix, require two approvers (one infra, one security), and we log a manual override entry in the change board (Doc: DocuSign link).

If Assess Partners wants raw token exchange traces, we need Legal review before sharing; ping me and I'll open the request.

— Marissa
Platform Security

Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: SIG evidence package for commit provenance & CI delegation (Greenline Financial)

Elena — attaching the package for Greenline's SIG intake. Attachments included in this email: signed-commits-snapshot.tar.gz, ci-job-ids-2026-Q1.csv, vault-rotation-log-2026-04.pdf, artifact-manifest-20260520.csv, deployment-policy-ephemeral-runners.md.

Summary of what we sent (short narrative):
- Commit provenance: We included a CSV of signed commits plus exported signatures. Pushes to main and release branches require either a GPG-signed merge or SSO-based signed merge through GitHub. We maintain verification metadata in git-notes and record signer key IDs; verification steps are documented in the README inside the tarball.
- CI gating: Release pipelines include required checks (static analysis, unit tests, integration smoke, artifact notarization). The manifest maps artifacts to job_ids and the ci-job CSV highlights the pipeline names and required check failures (if any).
- Secrets & runners: Vault transit logs show token minting and key rotation; runner enrollment requires infra-admin approval and uses short-lived tokens with TTL ~5 minutes. For emergency hotfixes we require the emergency/hotfix label and two approvers (infra + security) and record the manual override in the change board.

Follow-ups: if you need raw logs or additional signatures for specific SHAs, tell us which SHAs or job IDs and we'll provide a redaction plan prior to release. HubSpot deal: HS-94217.

Thanks — Soojin
Engineering Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

--
